text:
evan: Quick report — mobile sample app streaming sometimes shows joined JSON when app is backgrounded. looks like SSE `data:` lines split across TCP writes and later get concatenated incorrectly. repro steps in thread.
sarah: saw this on Android 11 emulator. raw capture: `data: {"id":7,"msg":"hi"}
data: {"id":8,"msg":"par"
` then next chunk `
data: "tial"}
` => id8.msg becomes `par"
"tial` which breaks parsing.
ken: sounds like proxy coalescing/chunk-splitting. fastly/edge-proxy can split arbitrarily. server should not assume one write == one SSE line.
sarah: current client logic auto-joins any bytes until blank line. that causes mixing when boundaries cut mid-JSON.
ev: proposal: server emits a sentinel `_fragment` event on socket close when `data:` line is unterminated, like `event: _fragment
data: <base64>

`. clients can opt-in to decode and reassemble by seq id. also add configurable heartbeat `event: hb` every 10s to avoid proxies treating idle as EOF.
ken: SDK parity: JS auto-joins, Go exposes onPartial. we should add an opt-in `sse.partial_policy` with options `auto_join` (default), `emit_fragment_event`, `callback_partial`. document and roll behind feature flag.
infra-bot: created task: FRAG-2026 (https://goto/tasks/FRAG-2026) to add sentinel fragments + heartbeat + e2e.
devx-bot: checklist: 1) runtime PR for fragment emission, 2) SDK flag & docs, 3) mobile e2e (background 20s), 4) correlate incidents.
sarah: i'll attach sampleapp trace and curl captures to FRAG-2026. ken: i'll start runtime PR and tag SDK owners. evan: thanks — will add minimal e2e and test on fastly staging.
